title: Double the Angle, Not the Sine Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Sin 30° is one half, so surely sin 60° is one? It is 0.866. Double again to 120° and the sine does not grow at all. So what really happens when you double an angle? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we derive the double-angle and triple-angle identities.

You will put y = x in the sum formula to get sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, then see the same fact as a picture: one triangle cut down the middle into two right triangles, same area both ways. A live graph shows sin 2x and 2 sin x splitting apart while 2 sin x cos x stays on the true curve. Then the three forms of cos 2x, tan 2x, the forms in tan x alone, and the triple-angle results sin 3x = 3 sin x - 4 sin³x and cos 3x = 4 cos³x - 3 cos x. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example (tan x = 3/4), the exam trap with the signs in cos 2x, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
